text.p: Middle-order pair Mark Waugh and Michael Bevan led Australia's recovery as West Indies wilted in the field in sweltering temperatures in the fifth and final test on Saturday.
Waugh and Beven batted through the afternoon session adding 120 runs in an unbroken fifth-wicket partnership after the home side were reduced to 49 for four before lunch on the opening day.
At tea at the WACA Ground, Australia were 169 for four, with Waugh unbeaten on 79 alongside Bevan on 50 not out.
But West Indies were hampered in their efforts by the extreme conditions in Perth, where the temperature soared to 46 degrees Celsius (115 degrees Fahrenheit) in the middle.
Fast bowlers Curtly Ambrose and Ian Bishop were clearly troubled by the heat during their bowling spells.
The tourists suffered a further blow when captain and fast-bowler Courtney Walsh was forced to leave the field with a hamstring injury.
Ambrose made an immediate impact on his return from injury to lift his side's spirits early on by removing opener Matthew Hayden for a duck and Steve Waugh for one before lunch.
Australia captain and opener Mark Taylor and number three Greg Blewett joined them in the pavilion as the West Indies tore through the top order.
It was a remarkable transformation for the tourists after their meek surrender in the fourth test in Adelaide as Australia took an unassailable 3-1 lead in the series.
Ambrose missed West Indies' crushing innings defeat at Adelaide Oval and his importance to the team was underlined by his bowling figures of two for 13 from 10 overs before lunch.
Hayden was dismissed without a run on the board and Australia sank into deeper trouble when Taylor was run out for two with the total on seven to prolong a run of low scores.
